text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VJESNIK
- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and his Bosnian counterpart Alija Izetbegovic will meet this month, says Foreign Minister Mate Granic in an interview.
- It is still an open question whether the U.N. or the newly-elected local authorities will have more power in Eastern Slavonia after July 15, Granic said.
- Supreme Court acquitted Antun Gudelj, accused of killing the head of the Osijek police at the beginning of the Serb rebellion in Croatia in 1991, Josip Reihl-Kir.

- Some 3,000 square metres of Croatian territory were covered by land mines during the war. Demining will last some ten years, says Damir Cemerin, managing director of the firm appointed by the government to clear mines.
- Food concern Vindija from Varazdin is the first food company in Croatia to introduce quality systems ISO 9001 amd HACCP, which opens the gate to the international market.
- State-owned insurer Croatia Osiguranje d.d. says it has turned around after five years of decline and recorded a 7.3 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 34.3 million kuna.
- Croatian tennis star Iva Majoli will play in the semi-finals of the French Open. She defeated Romania's Ruxandra Dragomir in quarter-finals 6-3, 5-7, 6-2.
VECERNJI LIST
- Less than 15 percent of Bosnian Croats have registered to vote in the Bosnian local elections in September. Registration deadline is June 16.

- Croatia expects 4.5 to 4.7 million tourists this summer, or 27 million overnights, which will mean some 15 million kuna foreign currency income, head of Croatia's Tourist Association Marijan Bulat said at the Croatian Economic Forum in Osijek.
- Bosnia is hiding documents which could lead to the acquittal of Bosnian Croat General Tihomir Blaskic, who is in the custody of the U.N. war crimes tribunal in The Hague.

- Introduction of euro as a common European currency will have huge consequences for the Croatian economy since more than half of Croatia's foreign trade is with European Union member countries, Deutsche bank experts warn.
- Drugs firm Pliva is a serious candidate to take part in the privatisation of part of Krakow's pharmaceutical company Polf, Polish sources say.
- There were 17,822 insolvent companies in February, or 1.46 percent more than in January. Their debts totalled 8.56 billion kuna, up 5.95 percent.
- The average monthly salary totalled 2,271 kuna in March, up 14.2 percent from the same month last year.
- Industrial output is on the rise and will continue to grow in the months ahead at a monthly rate of 0.5 percent in June and 0.19 percent in July, analysis from the City Trust Research Centre shows.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA

- President Franjo Tudjman will open a 16-kilometre long stretch of the highway linking Cakovec and Goricani, part of Europe's new corridor number five that connects Baltic countries and Eastern Europe with the Adriatic.
- Dubrovnik had 88,400 tourist overnights from January to May 1997.

- From a small local bank on the brink of collapse, we became a respectable Croatian bank, says head of the Dalmatinska Banka managing board Neven Dobrovic. The bank posted net profit of 14.7 million kuna in 1996.
- The U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) will provide $650,000 for rebuilding a railway line linking eastern Croatia and northern Bosnia. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
